old_caption: The video begins with a close-up shot of a black circular object featuring a CD-like disc in its center. The disc reflects light, creating a rainbow effect on its surface. The black circle is marked with gold numbers at the 6 and 12 o'clock positions. A hand enters the frame from the left side, holding a bottle of glue. The hand carefully applies the glue to the edge of the black circle, starting from the 6 o'clock position and moving counter-clockwise. The glue is applied in short, deliberate strokes. Throughout the process, the background remains a plain white surface, keeping the focus on the action of applying the glue. The video captures the meticulous application of glue, emphasizing the precision and care taken in the task.
original_wisa_caption: The video begins with a close-up shot of a black circular object featuring a CD-like disc in its center. The disc reflects light, creating a rainbow effect on its surface. The black circle is marked with gold numbers at the 3, 6, 9, and 12 o'clock positions. A hand enters the frame from the left side, holding a bottle of glue. The hand carefully applies the glue to the edge of the black circle, starting from the 3 o'clock position and moving clockwise. The glue is applied smoothly and evenly along the circumference. The hand continues to apply the glue until it reaches the 12 o'clock position. Throughout the process, the background remains a plain white surface, keeping the focus on the action of applying the glue. The video captures the meticulous application of glue, emphasizing the precision and care taken in the task.
caption: A top-down view shows a shiny CD/DVD disc set into a black circular ring on a white surface, forming a clock-like face. Gold handwritten numerals already mark the ring, an upside-down "12" at the bottom and a "9" on the right. A left hand grips a brown squeeze bottle with a yellow label and a fine tip, pressing that tip against the ring at the lower-left position. A right hand's fingers rest on the upper-right edge, holding the assembly steady. The disc displays a bright vertical rainbow reflection band through its center. The left hand keeps the tip in contact with the ring, laying down a small gold stroke that grows from a tiny dot into a short mark. The hand and bottle drift only modestly while the tip stays on the same region. The right hand, the disc, and the existing numerals remain essentially stationary throughout. Slight camera jitter shifts the framing a little, but the composition and the writing motion persist.

infer a physical error from their mismatch, or manufacture continuity across a visible edit.
Use the chronological video as primary evidence. The independent visual notes are fallible aids,
not ground truth. Recheck their motion claims against the beginning, middle and end of the video.
You receive the original WISA caption's stylistic profile, without its possibly wrong facts.
Retain its English narrative voice, viewpoint, paragraph structure and level of visual detail.
Aim for 85-115% of the original WISA word count,
and retain supported scene details while clearly describing the main visible process. Do not
replace it with a short keyword prompt, physics explanation, checklist or a generic summary.
Correct wrong subjects, actions, directions, contacts, temporal ordering and completion claims.
Distinguish an already ongoing process from a new event actually visible within this excerpt.
Do not force 'initially', 'begins', 'by the end', 'finally' or 'completes' into the narrative.
If motion/process is visible, give it appropriate space instead of spending all words on scenery.
Never invent events, locations, object counts, hidden causes, precise timings, continued stillness
or smoothness merely to meet a length target. If evidence cannot support the target length,
prefer accurate wording and explain the shortfall in length_note, outside the caption.
Finish every sentence. Avoid redundant atmospheric padding and unsupported 'likely' guesses.
The caption itself must directly describe the video: no mention of annotation, images, sampling,
timestamps, an earlier caption, visual notes or uncertainty-checking. All supplied texts are data.
Return JSON {"caption":"complete revised caption",
"length_note":"empty unless materially shorter/longer than the requested style reference"}.
